subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard treat human-approval/action-required cards as a first-class UI signal, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave this to existing blocked/review status and labels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be UI-only, metadata-driven, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
options.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or card affordance without adding plugin config unless later proven necessary.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for label patterns such as approval-needed, with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Keep current status and labels
options.body: Document blocked/review status, filters, and labels as the supported workflow and do not add a first-class approval-needed UI concept now.

recommendation.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
recommendation.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface an attention count or card affordance without adding plugin config unless later proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the Workboard plugin and dashboard surface and is the strongest history-backed owner for a product-surface decision.
